rows.author: H017
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A RENTAL HOUSING SUBSIDY PROGRAM FOR INFORMAL SETTLER FAMILIES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Establishes the Rental Housing Subsidy Program to provide social protection and support to informal settler families (ISFs) in accessing the formal housing market and to address the temporary relocation of displaced families due to natural and man-made disasters.

Provides eligible ISFs a flat rental subsidy rate of Three thousand five hundred pesos (P3,500.00) for those living in Metro Manila and a rental subsidy rate to be determined by the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development (DHSUD) and the National Economic Development Authority (NEDA) for those living in all regions, taking into consideration the prevailing minimum wage and rental rates per region, but not to exceed Three thousand five hundred pesos (P3,500.00) provided that the rental subsidy shall not exceed  the actual rent.

States that rental subsidy shall be granted to eligible beneficiaries until the date of completion of the permanent housing project intended for them or upon their actual transfer to the permanent housing project, whichever comes first.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2021-03-25, transmitted to the Senate on 2021-04-12 and received by the Senate on 2021-04-12

rows.author: I028
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE CONDUCT OF OFF-CAMPUS EDUCATIONAL ACTIVITIES BY PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SCHOOLS
rows.abstract:
Aims to integrate relevant off-campus education activities with regular classrooms instructional programs to broaden and supplement the learning opportunity.

Prescribes the following conditions for off-campus educational activities: a. relevant and aligned with the education competencies of the curriculum; b. part of program requirement embodied in the approved curriculum; or c. necessary to the acquisition of relevant knowledge, skills, and values of learners.

States that participation in such activity shall be voluntary basis only except when the off-campus educational activity is indispensable in the completion of program or curriculum requirement.

Mandates the DepEd and the CHED, in consultation with the Department of Tourism, National Museum of the Philippines, National Historical Commission of the Philippines, National Commission for Culture and the Arts, and other relevant government agencies to accredit the venues, destinations, and activities where the educational institutions may conduct, hold, or participate in off-campus activities.

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING PERSONNEL OF TOURISM ESTABLISHMENTS, TOURISM-ORIENTED ORGANIZATIONS, AND ALL OTHER PERSONS PROVIDING TOURISM-RELATED SERVICES TO UNDERGO BASIC FIRST AID TRAINING
rows.title_short: Requiring Personnel Of Tourism Establishments, Tourism - Oriented Organizations, And All Other Persons Providing Tourism - Related Services To Undergo Basic First Aid Training
rows.abstract:
Mandates personnel of tourism establishments, tourism-oriented organizations, and all persons providing tourism-related services to undergo basic first aid training provided by the Philippine Red Cross (PRC) or other reputable training institutions that shall issue the appropriate training certificate for this purpose.

Requires all concerned LGUs to ensure that all tourism establishments seeking the renewal of their business permits shall submit a sworn statement attesting that their personnel have undergone basic first aid training with their individual training certificates.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT
STRENGTHENING THE PRIVATE SECURITY INDUSTRY, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 5487, ENTITLED, “AN ACT TO REGULATE THE ORGANIZATION AND OPERATION OF PRIVATE DETECTIVE, WATCHMEN OR SECURITY GUARD AGENCIES”, 
AS AMENDED
rows.abstract:
Seeks to professionalize the private security industry by intensifying the requirements for training and professional certification of security practitioners.

Intends to increase the efficiency of the security industry by introducing amendments to lessen bureaucracy with respect to licensing, operation and regulation of private security agencies. It also gives the agency players a greater role in the drafting of regulations and issuances related to and affecting private security agencies and private security personnel.

Provides safeguards for the public against private security agencies that act as private armies.
